```json
{
  "winner": "A",
  "reasons": [
    "Distribution and billing are built in. A sells inside the Shopify App Store, where merchants are already shopping for apps. The brief gives a sourced paid channel that can start at $5/day, with one developer reporting cost per install about one third of other ad networks. B relies on Product Hunt and SEO. The brief itself calls those channels crowded with recent near-identical launches, and Instatus's SEO moat would take years to match.",
    "A has a gap the free incumbent does not cover. Shopify Magic is free, but the brief sources that it does not do alt text, images, titles, or bulk editing. That leaves a clear paid niche: vision-based, bulk, alt-text work with an ADA-compliance angle. B's only stated wedge is being cheaper, in a market where the brief says 10+ clones are already racing to $9/mo.",
    "A has lower operational risk for one person. A brief outage in a description generator is an annoyance. In B, reliability is existential: false alerts or downtime defeat the product, and the brief notes this requires multi-region infrastructure.",
    "A's demand quotes come from the target buyer. All three are merchants describing a chore they put off. B's quotes come mostly from developers who built their own monitor to avoid paying. That shows price sensitivity and a do-it-yourself instinct, not willingness to pay a new entrant.",
    "A's pricing anchors are sourced to live listings at $12–$130/mo, a range at or above B's realistic $9–15/mo entry tier."
  ],
  "weakest_evidence_in_loser": "The claim that 'a lone builder can reach meaningful MRR (Hyperping ~$15K...)' carries no source, so it counts as missing. Instatus's $40K MRR is only 'reported,' and the citation in the table is a pricing page, not a revenue source. The remaining demand quotes are written by people launching competing clones, which is evidence of supply, not buyers.",
  "confidence_note": "Moderate to low. Both ideas are saturated, and both briefs flag discovery, not building, as the bottleneck. A's own evidence has real holes. Recent entrants have almost no traction (0 and 3 reviews). Retention may collapse once a catalog is processed. The ADA settlement figures come from vendor and consultant blogs, not court data. A wins mainly on built-in distribution and lower reliability risk, not on strong proof of demand. A narrower alt-text and ADA product may be the better version of A."
}
```
